analysis.title: How will Fed rate hikes impact markets?
key_insights: UBS CIO expects the Fed to raise rates by 25bp in December 2026 and March 2027. The risk of consecutive hikes has grown.
October US inflation came in stronger than expected: headline CPI +0.4% m/m, core +0.3% m/m. UBS says this reinforces the case for tightening.
The FOMC held the fed funds target unchanged in October after raising it by 25bp in September.
UBS expects resilient growth and robust earnings to let US equities withstand a measured tightening cycle. It cites GDP growth near 2.5% annualized in 1H 2026 and 3.4% in Q3.
UBS forecasts S&P 500 earnings growth of 25% in 2026 and 14% in 2027, which it says should help equities absorb moderately higher yields.
UBS recommends staying positioned for further equity gains while diversifying across regions, sectors and return drivers, and managing concentrated single-stock exposure.
UBS rates fixed income Attractive and favors short- to medium-duration high-quality bonds to add portfolio income. It is cautious on the longest maturities.

Fed officials turned more hawkish over the past week. Dallas Fed President Logan suggested the pace of tightening might need to accelerate, and Governor Waller raised the possibility of a 50bp hike in December.
The 10-year Treasury yield hit 5.36% intraday in early October, the highest since 2002, and has since eased to about 5.13%.
The ISM Manufacturing PMI has been in expansion territory for ten consecutive months. UBS notes past US downturns generally began at least two years after the Fed started hiking.
earnings_insights: UBS forecasts S&P 500 earnings growth of 25% for 2026 and 14% for 2027 (UBS forecasts, not reported figures).

tension_points.bull_case: Resilient growth (Q3 GDP 3.4% annualized) and 2026 S&P 500 earnings growth forecast at 25% should let US equities absorb a measured tightening cycle.
tension_points.bear_case: Hotter October CPI and hawkish Fed comments (Logan on pace, Waller on a possible 50bp December hike) raise the risk of consecutive or larger hikes, which would exceed the measured path.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Consecutive hikes or a larger-than-25bp move such as the 50bp Waller raised for December would go beyond the measured tightening UBS assumes.
